# Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq snap 3-day losing streak as bonds rally, Moderna skyrockets

[Grace O'Donnell](https://finance.yahoo.com/author/grace-odonnell)· Editor, Special Projects

Updated Wed, August 19, 2026 at 4:07 PM EDT2 min read

- [MRNA \\
+176.97%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRNA/ "MRNA")

- [^DJI \\
+0.22%](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/ "^DJI")

- [^IXIC \\

US stocks rose on Wednesday, snapping a three-day losing streak, after the [US Treasury Department said](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607) it would increase its buybacks of long-dated government debt, leading yields to pull back sharply.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( [^DJI](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EDJI/)) and the S&P 500 ( [^GSPC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EGSPC/)) both gained 0.2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( [^IXIC](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EIXIC/)) also roughly put on 0.2%.

In individual stocks, Moderna ( [MRNA](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRNA/)) shares surged 176% after the company [reported positive results](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/moderna-shares-soar-60-on-melanoma-vaccine-trial-success-113706098.html) from its late-stage trial of a melanoma vaccine developed with Merck ( [MRK](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MRK/)).

53,463.05 +119.65 (+0.22%)

At close: August 19 at 4:38:37 PM EDT

^DJI^IXIC ^GSPC

Stocks gained momentum after Treasury yields eased from their highest levels in years. Bond prices, which move inversely to yields, rallied after the [US Treasury Department said](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607) it would increase buybacks of long-dated government debt "by at least double" for securities from the 10-year to 30-year sector.

The 10-year yield ( [^TNX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETNX/)) fell by 5 basis points to 4.65%, while the 30-year yield ( [^TYX](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ETYX/)) declined by 9 basis points to 5.19% after hitting its highest level since 2007 earlier this week.

Investors also watched the trade front after Trump [posted on Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117119761850520698) late Tuesday night that he paused the 50% Canadian tariffs for three days "based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalization of documents, have a DEAL!"

The announcement came after [11th-hour talks](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/new-50-tariffs-on-canadian-goods-are-scheduled-to-take-effect-at-midnight-150239060.html) between Trump officials and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney's team. While experts have said the tariffs would have had limited economic ramifications, they represent a strong signal of upcoming negotiations for the US-Mexico-Canada Trade Agreement (USMCA).

[Fed meeting minutes](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/article/several-fed-officials-wanted-to-raise-rates-last-month-if-inflation-doesnt-come-down-more-of-them-see-hikes-184112729.html) released on Wednesday afternoon, meanwhile, showed several Federal Open Market Committee members favored raising interest rates at the central bank's policy meeting last month and said that raising rates may be necessary if inflation doesn't come down soon.

[**Stocks Hitch a Ride on the Bond Market's Rally**](https://www.barrons.com/livecoverage/stock-market-news-today-081926/card/stocks-hitch-a-ride-on-the-bond-market-s-rally-48n4XuI0VGZ4ln2bdnWI)

By

[Connor Smith](https://www.barrons.com/authors/connor-smith?mod=livecoverage_web)

The stock market rode the bond market's coattails en route to its first gain in four sessions.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 120 points, or 0.2%. The S&P 500 was up 0.2%. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.2%.

News that the Treasury Department will at least double the size of buyback operations for longer-duration bonds sent bond prices rallying.

The rally on the long end of the bond market sent the yield on the 10-year Treasury note down to 4.65%. The 30-year yield dropped to 5.19%. For the 30-year yield, it was the largest decline since Oct. 10, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

Selling in artificial intelligence infrastructure stocks continued, but the rest of the market managed modest gains. Magnificent Seven and software stocks also countered chip stock selling.

Health care, led by Moderna on a cancer vaccine breakthrough, and consumer discretionary and materials were the top sectors. Industrials and tech, which both have plenty of AI plays, were the biggest laggards.

Minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee highlighted the divide among central bankers on whether interest rates may need to be raised to fight inflation soon, but stocks mostly shrugged off the release.

# Stock Market Today (Aug. 19, 2026): S&P 500 rises despite tech weakness as health care, cyclicals jump

The Treasury Department said it will more than double the size of its debt buybacks, sending Treasury yields lower.

Aug 19, 2026 2:12 PM EDT

- ![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/MTkyMjg3NDQwMDY3NjM0NzM0/rob-lenihan.jpg?profile=w256&ar=1-1)


By [Rob Lenihan](https://www.thestreet.com/author/rob-lenihan) and [Noah Weidner](https://www.thestreet.com/author/noah-weidner)

Follow

0

[Add us on](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thestreet.com)

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTQwOTE1/procter-gamble-company_me_081026.jpg?profile=w2560&ar=4-3)[Spencer Platt / Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/82916776)

_This live blog is refreshed throughout the day with the latest updates from the market._ **_To find the latest [Stock Market Today](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/stock-market-today) threads, [click here](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/stock-market-today)._**

**Happy Wednesday.** Stocks rose Wednesday after the [Treasury Department](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/t/treasury-department) said it will more than double the size of its debt buybacks.

Global government bonds stabilized Wednesday following the steep selloff before the release of minutes from the [Federal Reserve](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/f/federal-reserve)’s July meeting. The minutes are scheduled for release at 2 p.m. EDT.

President Donald Trump said earlier that there are no ongoing talks with Iran and no new discussions scheduled, nearly six months into the war involving the U.S., Israel and Iran.

Separately, Trump late Tuesday paused plans to impose 50% tariffs on certain Canadian imports, shortly before the duties were set to take effect at midnight.

Stocks [closed lower Tuesday](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-aug-18-2026), pressured by a selloff in chipmakers and elevated bond yields.

“Chip stocks took a hit while rising bond yields weighed on asset prices around the world as investors became increasingly nervous about higher long-end rates,” said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com.

“The move in yields was relatively modest and partly unwound throughout the US session. But the cross-asset price action points to one of the big structural tensions in the markets right now bubbling to the surface again.”

Rodda said big government spending and, partly by extension, the [AI](https://www.thestreet.com/tag/artificial-intelligence) investment boom are driving significant competition for resources, creating greater scarcity, inflationary risks and a higher cost of capital.

“While this spending and investment is creating massive profits and therefore supporting higher share prices, the recycling of those earnings and increased borrowing by AI businesses into even greater spending and investment is fueling a feedback loop resulting in structurally higher yields,” he said.

Although market participants have been willing to stomach higher yields because future returns are expected to be worth it, Rodda said the rise in some parts of the [yield](https://www.thestreet.com/dictionary/y/yield) curve to multi-year or multi-decade highs has shaken confidence enough to force a slight re-rating of stocks.

10 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 2:12 PM EDT)

## S&P 500 Today: Health care, cyclicals lead pack

The **S&P 500**(+0.19%) remains up about a fifth of a percentage point heading towards the homestretch of trading, even despite the drag generated by tech, industrials, and financials. Thankfully, there’s plenty to celebrate in health care, where **Moderna**(+140%) and **Merck**(+12%) are having fantastic showings for the index today. Strength in consumer sectors and comm services are also helping keep the index afloat.

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTUwNDgz/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

11 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 12:43 PM EDT)

## Midday Movers: $MRNA, $TEM, $BNTX, $EL, $TWST lead

Biotech names are fetching plenty of attention after **Moderna’s**(+141%) big phase 3 results today. Here are the top 20 stocks in the market with at least a $2 billion market cap:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTUwMzQ4/screenshot-2026-08-19-at-9-57-22-am.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

12 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 11:46 AM EDT)

## Midday Movers: Semiconductor names lead the losers

Almost midway through the day, 35.6% of U.S. issues are declining, but there’s a decisive theme in today’s losers. Almost all of them are technology names. Here’s a look at the bottom 20 names in the market with at least a $2 billion market cap, which includes $VICR, $AEHR, $NBIS, and $AXTI, among others:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTUwMjM3/screenshot-2026-08-19-at-8-59-20-am.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

13 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 10:48 AM EDT)

## Moderna surges after successful cancer vaccine trial

**Moderna**(+121%) is the stock of the day after posting successful results from its phase 3 trial for its personalized cancer vaccine, a first of its kind treatment intended to prevent the recurrence of melanoma. This move is its best single-day showing in the company’s history.

Here’s the YTD for context:

![](https://www.thestreet.com/.image/NDA6MDAwMDAwMDAzMTUwMTgw/image.png?profile=w2560&x=50&y=50)

It’s far and away the best performer in the S&P 500 today, which is up about six-tenths of one percent. Today’s move makes it the second best performer in the index this year, up 355% year-to-date.

The news has lifted shares of **BioNTech**(+19.27%), which is pursuing a similar treatment, while two biotech ETFS — the $XBI and $IBB — are up over 4%.

By Rob Lenihan14 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 10:13 AM EDT)

## Market Movers: Moderna, Merck, CrowdStrike

Moderna (MRNA) skyrocketed nearly 111% after the company announced positive Phase 3 trial results with Merck (MRK) for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine combined with Keytruda in melanoma patients.

Estee Lauder (EL) soared 18.4% after the beauty brand reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that beat Wall Street estimates for both earnings and revenue, alongside a fiscal 2027 profit outlook that topped consensus expectations.

Merck (MRK) rose 11.2% after the company announced positive Phase 3 trial results with Moderna for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine combined with Keytruda in melanoma patients.

On the downside, shares of AI cloud company Nebius Group NV (NBIS) fell 12.7% after disclosing plans to raise $4.50 billion through a private offering of convertible senior notes, split between $2.75 billion of notes due in 2030 and $1.75 billion of notes due in 2034.

Dell (DELL) lost 7.2% amid profit-taking in the artificial intelligence hardware sector, lingering caution following recent Wall Street price-target adjustments and heavy insider selling.

CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) lost 7.1% as investors locked in profits ahead of the cybersecurity company’s Aug. 26 earnings report.

By Rob Lenihan15 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 9:34 AM EDT)

## Open Bell: Stocks Rise on Treasury Buybacks

**The U.S. stock market is now open.** Stocks were rising in early trading after the Treasury Department said it will more than double the size of its debt buybacks.

The S&P 500 gained 0.43%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.25%, and the Nasdaq climbed 0.40%. The Russell 2000 lost 1.30%.

By Rob Lenihan15 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 9:11 AM EDT)

## Treasury Department Says It Will Double Government Debt Buybacks

The Treasury Department on Wednesday said it [will more than double](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/treasury-announces-upscaled-buyback-operation-for-longer-term-debt-sending-yields-lower.html) the size of its government debt repurchases, CNBC reported, sending Treasury yields sharply lower.

With fixed-income markets under pressure and yields surging to levels not seen in nearly 20 years, the announcement targets a sensitive part of the Treasury market.

Under the accelerated buyback program, Treasury will target the 10- to 20-year and 20- to 30-year portions of the market, which have seen a buyers’ strike since late June.

The government will “at least double” the maximum size of its buyback operations, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion, according to an announcement from the department.

By Rob Lenihan15 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 8:49 AM EDT)

## Mag 7 Update: Magnificent Seven ETF Edges Lower Before the Bell

The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) edged down 0.03% to $66.80 in premarket trading.

The ETF tracks an equal-weight portfolio of seven major companies: Alphabet (GOOG), Amazon (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Meta Platforms (META), Microsoft (MSFT), Nvidia (NVDA), and Tesla (TSLA).

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 8:28 AM EDT)

## Premarket Movers: Moderna, Estée Lauder, Lowe’s

Moderna (MRNA) soared 105% after the company announced positive Phase 3 trial results with Merck (MRK) for a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine combined with Keytruda in melanoma patients.

Merck rose 8.3% on the news.

Estée Lauder (EL) gained 8% after the beauty brand reported fiscal fourth-quarter results that beat Wall Street estimates for both earnings and revenue, alongside a fiscal 2027 profit outlook that topped consensus expectations.

On the downside, Mercury Systems (MRCY) slumped 8.8% after the aerospace and defense electronics company missed Wall Street’s fourth-quarter earnings expectations.

Retailer TJX Cos. (TJX) lost 4.7% after its third-quarter profit forecast fell short of Wall Street estimates, despite reporting a second-quarter earnings and revenue beat.

Lowe’s Companies (LOW) fell 3.53% after the home improvement and hardware company gave a cautious full-year outlook, citing “pressure” in do-it-yourself (DIY) consumer spending.

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 7:58 AM EDT)

## Moderna Skyrockets on Cancer Vaccine Results

Moderna (MRNA) shares skyrocketed nearly 102% in premarket trading after an experimental personalized cancer vaccine developed with Merck (MRK) showed positive interim results in its first Phase 3 trial.

Merck shares were up 8.2%.

Moderna’s mRNA vaccine, combined with Merck’s immunotherapy Keytruda, met its goals in a late-stage trial for skin cancer, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/merck-moderna-say-melanoma-skin-cancer-vaccine-meets-goals-large-trial-2026-08-19/).

The study is ongoing, but interim results found the treatment, intismeran, met both its primary endpoint of reducing cancer recurrence and its secondary endpoint of keeping cancers from spreading to other parts of the body.

Moderna has been diversifying its portfolio beyond its COVID-19 vaccine. The company recently added an FDA-approved flu vaccine while developing experimental shots for diseases including norovirus and Lyme disease.

Last month, Barclays analysts said they expect the therapy could generate about $3 billion in melanoma treatment revenue by 2035.

By Rob Lenihan16 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 7:48 AM EDT)

## Iran War News: UAE Suspends Trade With Iran After Missile Launches

The United Arab Emirates said it had [paused all trade and financial transactions](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz.html) with Iran, according to CNBC, after reporting that two ballistic missiles were launched from Iran toward its territorial waters.

Both missiles fell into the water and caused no damage or casualties, the UAE said Wednesday.

However, the reported strike represents an unwelcome return of the conflict to the Gulf economy’s shores after more than three months.

Weeks of Iranian drone and missile attacks on the UAE earlier this year, the vast majority of which were intercepted, sparked tensions among locals and hammered the country’s tourism and aviation industries.

President Donald Trump on Tuesday confirmed the U.S. is not currently in talks with Iran and has no plans to restart them, a claim Tehran had already made. Trump also ruled out extending the 60-day ceasefire agreement, which expired Monday.

Oil prices have resumed climbing as negotiations have stalled.

By Rob Lenihan17 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 7:26 AM EDT)

## What is the price of silver on Wednesday, August 19, 2026?

Silver futures fell 0.78% to $63.54 an ounce in early trading.

By Rob Lenihan17 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 7:23 AM EDT)

## What is the price of gold on Wednesday, August 19, 2026?

## Target Shares Fall Despite Earnings Beat

Target (TGT) shares were down 2.44% in premarket trading even after the retailer beat Wall Street’s second-quarter earnings expectations and raised its annual sales forecast.

It was the third straight strong quarter for Target, which also raised its growth forecast in May.

“Second-quarter results build on the encouraging momentum we saw in the first quarter, giving us increasing confidence that our strategy is resonating with our guests and strengthening our leadership position in style, design, and value,” CEO Michael Fiddelke said in a statement.

“While there’s still meaningful work ahead, we’re encouraged by the progress we’re making and remain focused on executing with discipline, staying agile in a dynamic operating environment, and investing in our team and capabilities to drive sustainable, profitable growth over the long term.”

By Rob Lenihan17 hours ago (Aug 19, 2026 7:02 AM EDT)

## Oil Market Update: Prices Rise as Iran Peace Talks Stall

Oil prices were climbing after the two-month window for negotiations over a peace deal expired Monday with no end to the conflict between the U.S. and Iran in sight.

West Texas Intermediate crude surged 1.24% to $85.99 per barrel, while Brent crude rose 1.1% to $92 per barrel.

President Donald Trump has said the U.S. is not in any talks with Iran and has no plans to start new ones.

Wall Street closed lower on Tuesday, dragged down by tech and industrial stocks. Investor sentiment weakened as Middle East uncertainty drove bond yields to multiyear highs, raising concerns over inflation and borrowing costs. All three benchmark indexes ended in the red.

## How Did the Benchmarks Perform?

The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) lost 116.38 points, or 0.2%, to close at 53,343.4. Nineteen components of the 30-stock index ended in the positive territory, while 11 ended in the negative.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 355.2 points, or 1.3%, to close at 26,289.71.

The S&P 500 slid 53.3 points, or 0.7%, to close at 7,691.76. Seven of the 11 broad sectors of the benchmark index closed in the red. The Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK), the Industrials Select Sector SPDR (XLI) and the Materials Select Sector SPDR (XLB) declined 1.9%, 1.5% and 0.9%, respectively, while the Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) advanced 1.8%.

The fear gauge CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) increased 4.3% to 15.84. A total of 14.86 billion shares were traded on Tuesday, lower than the last 20-session average of 16.88 billion. Decliners outnumbered advancers by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.67-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

## Oil Continues to Climb as Middle East Tensions Persist

Oil prices settled at their highest levels in more than three weeks on Tuesday as Iran adopted a more offensive stance and said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed. The United States ruled out extending a ceasefire, adding to supply concerns. Brent crude gained 0.17% to $91.02 a barrel, while WTI crude rose 0.52% to $84.94, with both closing at their highest since July 24.

## Investor Sentiment Weakens as Bond Yields Rise

Investor sentiment turned cautious on Wall Street on Tuesday as heightened uncertainty surrounding the Middle East pushed Treasury yields to multiyear highs. The 30-year yield touched roughly 5.33%, its highest level since 2007, before easing slightly to around 5.29% by the close. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield hovered near 4.73%. The rise in borrowing costs renewed concerns that elevated energy prices and geopolitical risks could fuel inflation, potentially complicating the outlook for monetary policy.

Higher yields also made equities less attractive relative to fixed-income investments, adding pressure to risk appetite. Technology and semiconductor stocks bore much of the selling pressure, as investors remained particularly sensitive to higher financing costs and stretched valuations. The PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged about 5.6%, with all 30 components declining. The cautious mood reflected growing concerns that persistent inflationary pressures and geopolitical uncertainty could weigh on economic growth and corporate earnings. As a result, Wall Street's main indexes ended lower, extending a more defensive tone across the broader market.

## Economic Data

Per the U.S. Census Bureau and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Housing starts for July came in at 1,239,000. The number for June was revised down to 1,415,000 from the previously reported 1,427,000. The July number for Building Permits came in at 1,443,000, while the June number was revised up to 1,374,000 from the previously reported 1,367,000.

Per a Fed report, Industrial Production increased 0.2% in July. The number for June was revised up to 0.3% from the previously reported 0.1%. Capacity Utilization increased to 76.3 after rising to 76.2 in June.

Per the National Association of Realtors, Pending Home Sales fell 2.3% in July. The number for June was revised to a fall of 4.8% from the previously reported 5.4%.
